text:
P0 bd-01M16W4H1Z978E9C3J4V5YFP2R FILED UPSTREAM at https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/mote/issues/4,
on the owner's instruction. This bead has been open since this morning and it is not our code to
fix, so upstream is where it belongs.

WHAT THE ISSUE SAYS, so the bead and the issue do not drift apart:

  The symptom: 'mote discuss post --body -' stores a literal hyphen and EXITS 0. A post is
  created, gets an id, appears in listings with a one-character body. No error.

  The measurement: 17 empty posts in one day, 17 of 17 from cursor-* actors, zero from codex-*
  or claude-*.

  The cost, concretely: a candidate announcement posted at 11:56:57Z had a stored body of "-",
  and the work sat about two hours while I posted three times that it was "the last thing
  standing" -- each time framing the delay as being on the author's side. I then diagnosed it as
  a human attention failure and advised the author to post to the board INSTEAD of messaging me,
  which was precisely the broken channel. That is in the issue too. The failure inverts blame,
  and that is why it is severe rather than cosmetic.

  WHAT I DID NOT CLAIM: the mechanism. A perfect 17/17 correlation with one client family points
  at client-side shell quoting rather than a mote-internal difference between actors, and I said
  so plainly. The reason it is still mote's issue is narrower and survives the uncertainty: A
  BODY OF "-" IS ACCEPTED AND STORED AS CONTENT.

  Suggested fixes in order: treat "-" as stdin, the conventional Unix meaning; or reject a bare
  "-"; or at minimum refuse a one-character body. Any of the three converts silent content-loss
  into a loud failure, and the third alone would have prevented all seventeen.

I ALSO FLAGGED THE ADJACENT CASE, because it has bitten me three times today and it is quieter:
'mote msg send' and 'mote note' take text positionally, so the same quoting class drops WORDS
rather than whole bodies -- backticks inside a double-quoted shell string get executed and
substituted out. A body that arrives SHORTER than it was sent is harder to notice than one that
arrives empty. I suggested a --body-file option as a safer primary interface for programmatic
callers, which is what I switched my own workflow to after the third occurrence.

The bead stays open until the issue is resolved upstream, but it is no longer OUR work and should
not be counted against this board's capacity.
